lines: Chicago blamed its Great Fire on a cow.
In October 1871, a fire broke out in the O'Learys' barn.
It killed about 300 people and left 100,000 homeless.
Newspapers said Mrs. O'Leary's cow kicked over a lantern.
Years later, a reporter claimed he had made that up.
In 1997, the city council officially cleared her, and the cow.
Today, the city trains its firefighters right where the O'Learys lived.

youtube.title: Chicago blamed its Great Fire on a cow. It was framed
youtube.description:
The Great Chicago Fire broke out on the night of October 8, 1871, in or near the barn of Patrick and Catherine O'Leary on DeKoven Street; it killed about 300 people and left some 100,000 homeless, about a third of the city. Newspapers spread the story that Mrs. O'Leary's cow had kicked over a lantern, although she testified that she was in bed and the official inquiry could not determine the cause. Michael Ahern, a reporter for the Chicago Republican, later claimed he had made up the cow story, and in 1997 the Chicago City Council passed a resolution exonerating Catherine O'Leary and her cow. Since 1961, the Chicago Fire Academy has stood on the old O'Leary property.

Sources: Smithsonian Magazine, "What (or Who) Caused the Great Chicago Fire?"; History.com, "Chicago Fire of 1871"; Chicago History Museum and Northwestern University, "The O'Leary Legend" (greatchicagofire.org); Chicago Public Library, "Whodunit? The Mystery of Mrs. O'Leary's Cow"; City of Chicago, "Site of the Chicago Fire" (1971 landmark summary); Wikipedia, "Catherine O'Leary".
Images: Library of Congress, public domain / no known restrictions: "Chicago in Flames: Scene at Randolph Street Bridge" and "The Great Fire at Chicago, Octr. 8th 1871" (Currier & Ives); "The Great Fire at Chicago Oct. 9th 1871, View from the West Side" (Gibson & Co.); "Origin of the Chicago Fire" (1871, after a painting by L.V.H. Crosby); stereographs of the ruins (P.B. Greene) and of Mrs. O'Leary's residence (J. Mountford), 1871; Daily Kennebec Journal, October 31, 1871 (Chronicling America); Chicago City Hall (Historic American Buildings Survey).

translation_es: Chicago le echó la culpa de su Gran Incendio a una vaca. En octubre de 1871, se desató un incendio en el granero de los O'Leary. Mató a unas 300 personas y dejó a 100.000 sin casa. Los diarios dijeron que la vaca de la señora O'Leary pateó un farol. Años después, un periodista aseguró que eso lo había inventado él. En 1997, el concejo de la ciudad la declaró inocente oficialmente, a ella y a la vaca. Hoy, la ciudad entrena a sus bomberos justo donde vivían los O'Leary. Aun así, durante 126 años… Chicago le echó la culpa de su Gran Incendio a una vaca.
why_es: Es un mito que casi todos en EE.UU. conocen, pero muy pocos saben que la vaca fue "absuelta" oficialmente en 1997 y que la academia de bomberos está en ese mismo terreno.
